patches.purpose: Give a reopened task a normal task-bound stage: wake the same assignee on a closed -> in_progress reopen, never treat a previous stage run that recorded Done/In Review/Blocked as an undisposed run, and never let a summary written before the current stage park it, reading every summary representation from one identified revision so its writer's own status write cannot unpark it; and keep an addressed Coordinator wake from being stranded: re-drain the deferred queue after a dispatch-gate cancellation, retire a deferred addressed-card wake whose invitation left pending, and report that cancellation as interaction_no_longer_pending instead of a reassignment; and persist that re-drain as a durable intent with the gate cancellation, consumed post-commit and by the restart sweep for any addressee and settled only from its persisted outcome; deciding every part of that drain (intent, Stop, never-started exemption, queue interrupt, snapshot, settlement) from the run row locked under the issue lock, holding the intent pending when that row changed underneath.
retirementRequires: Relevant regressions run against exact upstream SHA WITHOUT this patch; pass results retained.
Fresh independent review confirms upstream covers the original behavior and protected boundaries.
Final combined candidate exact-head CI and runtime qualification pass.
patches.notes: Carried on maintenance/guarded-upgrade-setup, not on the repair line fix/network-proxy-child-stdio; 53373965 and its R7 follow-up 6e5f6590 are self-contained server commits (code plus regressions), selected together onto the repair line for a later qualified installation. Reproduced from STA-22 round 8 native records: comment cd8268d7 landed on a Done task, a separate PATCH reopened it done -> in_progress with no wake, and the stranded sweep dispatched issue_disposition_repair run 9dab77f6 against previous-stage run 0bf7baf2 (recovery action 774502e5). Stage boundaries come from structured issue.updated audit rows (run_id, details.status, details.changes.status or details._previous.status), not summary prose. The route regression runs from a port of upstream's own harness file; see maintenance/upgrade/ports/native-task-bound-continuation/PORT.md. The Postgres regressions need embedded Postgres; a host that cannot start it skips them, which is unknown. Run with --isolation private-network-user. R7 (STA-22 round 9): queued summary snapshots now name their revision, and live and queued summaries share one predicate that takes body, time and writer from that revision; missing or invalid provenance keeps the park. Stage 9 (FAC-760 STA-43, founder 3b8f05fe; card eb807dc7): 37b2bf5b re-drains the deferred queue in a drain-only mode when the claim gate cancels a run (no recovery, no blocked projection, no legacy hold when that run row never started), retires a deferred interaction_pending wake whose invitation is no longer pending, and cancels such a run as interaction_no_longer_pending. The Postgres file drives the real wake-queue release and the real heartbeat claimQueuedRun gate; it needs embedded Postgres. Stage 10 (STA-22 round 11 R8, checkpoint ec6285d5 option B; card e09877a9): the claim gate writes resultJson.gateCancellationDrain on the cancelled run in the same transaction as the cancellation (no schema change), naming the deferred wakes then queued; the release consumes it under the issue then run locks (post-commit and resumeQueuedRuns, for any addressee), drains only those wakes, and settles it from what it persisted: promoted successor, no snapshot wake still deferred, or another lock holder. A bare released outcome never settles it; a held intent stays pending. The never-started exemption now requires that persisted intent. Regressions: native-gate-cancellation-drain.test.ts (real claim gate, release and restart sweep on Postgres). Stage 11 (STA-22 round 12 R9; card f445ebd5): on a gate-cancellation release the run row read FOR UPDATE under the issue lock is the only source for the intent, every pre-drain fact (Stop and native Stop receipts, the queue-interrupt override, the never-started exemption), the snapshot handed to the drain and its caller, and settlement; the unlocked first read only chooses the issue locks. If the locked row's status or task differs from that first read, a pending intent stays pending (heldReason run_row_changed). Regressions: a separate connection holds the issue row lock so the release stops after its first read, commits the change, then releases it (describe "run row changed between the release's first read and its locked read (R9)").

patches.notes: FAC-760 STA-21 stage 12 (Coordinator disposition cd0354d8, card 6b2a12f5). Runs 19befcbc and d79920b9 (the only runs live 20:29-21:03Z, same server boot 0c006597, no lease revocation) ended provider success -> cancelled/unknown. Local adapters ignore the host abort signal; of the host abort sites only the lease watchdog writes nothing. Not carried: upstream private liveness-pool renewal, statement-timeout retry and pre-dispatch controller_lease_lost failure code; the live loss cause is unrecorded, so they are not shown to fix it. Upstream already contains this behaviour, so the expected proposal is retire on upgrade once upstream-only regressions and independent review confirm it. The host file needs embedded Postgres; a host that cannot start it skips, which is unknown. Run with --isolation private-network-user.

requiredCiJobsNote: Every lane of the reviewed expected CI graph (maintenance/ci-graph.json), regenerated from the candidate's exact workflow blobs: its pull_request workflows, the PR base branch's pull_request_target workflows and each immutable reusable workflow. Admission requires this set to equal the graph's lanes (R4: an aggregate such as `ci / verify` does not prove the lanes it does not need), and every observed check must also succeed. Path- or branch-filtered workflows are recorded as conditional: their checks must succeed when present but are not expected. Any change to a workflow blob changes the graph and needs fresh review.
